# Herdr Worklist: Track Agents Spawned per Work Item and Show Their Status Icon

## Problem statement

When a user spawns a pi agent from the herdr worklist (via `/intake`, `/plan`, or `/skill:*` on a selected work item), the worklist has no knowledge of that agent afterwards. There is no way to see, directly in the list, that an agent is attached to a particular work item or what state that agent is in — even though the herdr sidebar already tracks this (idle / working / blocked).

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** — Anyone who spawns agents from the worklist and wants to see, at a glance, which work items currently have an agent attached and what state that agent is in.

Example user stories:

- "As a worklist user, when I spawn an agent on `WL-XXXX` from the list, I want that row to show an icon reflecting the agent's status so I can see which items have active agents without switching panes."
- "As a worklist user, when the agent pane closes, I want the icon to disappear immediately so the list reflects reality."
- "As a worklist user, I want the agent icon's presence or absence to never shift the other icons or the item-ID column, so the list stays readable."
- "As a worklist user, when I restart the plugin or open a second worklist tab, I want the agent-to-work-item mapping to still be known."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an agent command (`/intake`, `/plan`, `/skill:*`) carrying a work-item ID is dispatched from the worklist, the plugin records the work-item ↔ agent-pane association (capturing the new pane ID from the spawn flow) before/while spawning the agent.
2. The list shows an agent-status icon at the **start of the icon prefix** for every row whose work item has a tracked agent, reflecting the agent's current state (`idle` / `working` / `blocked`) using the same state values the herdr sidebar shows.
3. **Alignment invariance:** the agent icon occupies a fixed-width reserved slot in the icon prefix. Rows with and without an agent icon keep the status/stage/review icons and the item-ID column at identical columns (unit test asserts no column shift).
4. The mapping persists across plugin restarts in a gitignored JSON state file (e.g. `.worklog/agent-panes.json`) and is shared across worklist panes/tabs.
5. When the agent pane is gone (closed/exited), the entry is pruned and the icon disappears on the next refresh cycle.
6. Only agents spawned from the worklist's agent commands are tracked; manually opened pi agent panes and commands without a work-item ID are not tracked.
7. Status lookup fails open: when the `herdr` CLI/socket is unavailable or an error occurs, no icons are rendered and the list continues to function normally (matching the existing `visibility.ts` fail-open pattern).
8. Unit tests cover: tracker record/prune/persistence, agent-state → icon mapping, fixed-slot alignment, and dispatch-time association capture.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and the herdr agent-state protocol doc if relevant.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.

## Constraints

- Must work with the existing `send-to-pi.sh` flow. The shared script (`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`) is consumed by other plugins (e.g. `herdr-podcast-editor` via git submodule), so any change must be **backward compatible** (new optional flag only).
- The plugin currently spawns `send-to-pi.sh` detached with `stdio: ignore`; pane-ID capture must not block the TUI event loop or change spawn behavior for other routes.
- Status refresh should reuse the `PollGate` TTL-memoizer pattern from `src/visibility.ts` to avoid `herdr` CLI spawn churn on every render tick.
- The state file must live in a gitignored location (`.worklog/` is already ignored).
- The planned Rust migration (WL-0MS8XGSE400374VS) means the TS implementation should be self-contained and portable (pure functions where feasible).
- Follow the existing icon conventions in `src/icons.ts` (emoji + `[TEXT]` fallback, `stringDisplayWidth` for width math).

## Existing state

- `src/index.ts` `onCommand` routes agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`) to `scripts/send-to-pi.sh`, spawned **detached with stdio ignored**. The work-item ID is extracted via `extractWorkItemId()` and the item is claimed (`claimWorkItem`) before spawn, but the **new pane ID is discarded** — the script parses it internally and never surfaces it.
- Row rendering: `formatItemLine()` in `src/worklist.ts` composes each row via `getIconPrefix()` in `src/icons.ts`, which concatenates status → stage/audit → review → epic icons and pads to a fixed 12-cell width (`ICON_PREFIX_WIDTH`).
- `WorkItem` (src/fetcher.ts) has no agent-related field.
- The herdr CLI exposes agent status per pane: `herdr agent list` / `herdr agent get <pane_id>` return `agent_status` (observed values: `working`, `done`; protocol/CLI states: `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `unknown`). The work-item association cannot be recovered from `herdr pane process-info` (cmdline is just `pi`), so it must be recorded at spawn time.

## Desired change

1. **`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`** (+ `scripts/send-to-pi.sh` passthrough): add an optional `--pane-id-file <path>` flag that writes the new pane ID immediately after `herdr pane split` succeeds. Backward compatible; absent flag = current behavior.
2. **New `src/agent-tracker.ts`**: in-memory + persisted (`.worklog/agent-panes.json`, atomic write) mapping `workItemId → paneId`; `recordAgentForWorkItem()`, pruning of entries whose pane no longer exists (via `herdr agent get`/`agent list`), and a cached `refreshStates()` returning `Map<workItemId, 'idle'|'working'|'blocked'|'done'>`. Fail-open on herdr errors.
3. **`src/index.ts`**: on agent-command dispatch, pass `--pane-id-file <tmpfile>` to the spawn; a fire-and-forget async task polls briefly for the file, reads the pane ID, and records the mapping. Never blocks the TUI.
4. **`src/fetcher.ts`**: add optional `agentState?: 'idle' | 'working' | 'blocked' | 'done'` to `WorkItem`; merge tracker state into fetched items (in fetcher or TUI refresh cycle).
5. **`src/icons.ts`**: add `agentStatusIcon(state, opts)`; `getIconPrefix()` gains a **fixed-width first slot** (2 cells, icon or blank) for the agent status so the remaining icons never shift.
6. **Tests**: `src/agent-tracker.test.ts` (new), icon-alignment tests, dispatch-association tests in `src/index.test.ts`/`worklist.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — NEW: mapping store, persistence, pruning, status refresh (PollGate-cached, fail-open)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — capture pane ID on agent dispatch (`--pane-id-file`) and record association
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — optional `--pane-id-file` flag (backward compatible)
- `packages/herdr/scripts/send-to-pi.sh` — pass through `--pane-id-file`
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — `agentStatusIcon()` + fixed-width agent slot in `getIconPrefix()`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — pass `agentState` through to icon prefix (`formatItemLine`)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `WorkItem.agentState` field; state merge
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.test.ts` — NEW: record/prune/persist/refresh tests
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` / `index.test.ts` — alignment + dispatch-association tests
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the new icon and behavior

## Related work

- `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — defines `pane.report_agent` and the sidebar states (`idle`, `working`, `blocked`) this feature mirrors.
- WL-0MS9NPHQU005Y3VE (completed) — "Herdr plugin should set work-item status to in_progress when instigating actions": same dispatch path; established `extractWorkItemId()` + claim-before-spawn. This feature extends that flow by capturing the pane ID.
- WL-0MS5CDIR1008VRTN (completed) — "Open pi agent pane for skill commands sent from herdr worklist": established the `send-to-pi.sh` dispatch mechanism.
- WL-0MS8XGSE400374VS (open) — "Migrate ContextHub herdr plugin to Rust": planned migration; TS work should be portable/self-contained.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (open) — "Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn": adjacent refresh-caching concern; PollGate reuse reduces overlap.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Icon glyph mapping:** confirmed by user — `working → 🟢` (green circle), `blocked → ⛔` (no-entry sign, user's stated preference), `idle → ⚪` (white circle, default if a state must be shown). `done`/pane-closed → no icon. Text fallbacks follow the `[TEXT]` convention.
- **Pane-ID capture race**: `--pane-id-file` may never appear if the split fails; tracker treats a missing pane as a no-op (no entry recorded). Icon appears on the next refresh after recording.
- **Persistence concurrency**: multiple worklist tabs writing `.worklog/agent-panes.json` — atomic write (write-temp-then-rename) plus last-writer-wins is acceptable; avoid holding file locks.
- **Stale entries**: an entry whose pane closes while the plugin is not running is pruned on the next refresh; `done` status may linger for one refresh before removal.
- **Scope-creep guard**: do NOT add sidebar-style agent panels, per-item agent history, or agent output previews. If desired, record as separate linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the worklist row icon mirror the sidebar's exact glyphs/colors, or is a status icon consistent with the worklist's existing emoji style (with text fallback) acceptable?" — Answer (user): "no entry sign (preference), or red circle. Go for consistency." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: use the worklist's existing emoji icon style; glyph preference ⛔ or 🔴. **Follow-up clarification:** "make working a green circle" — Answer (user): working → 🟢 (green circle). Source: interactive reply. Final mapping: `working → 🟢`, `blocked → ⛔`, `idle → ⚪`, `done`/pane-closed → no icon.
- Q2: "Which agents to track — only worklist-spawned agent commands, or also manually opened pi agent panes working in the same project?" — Answer (user): "only worklist spawned". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the mapping persist across plugin restarts, and should the icon disappear as soon as the agent pane closes?" — Answer (user): "yes persist, disappear immediately". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (follow-up): "When the agent icon is/is not present, alignment of other icons should not be affected" — Answer (user): "Note, when the icon is/is not present the alignment of other icons should not be affected". Source: interactive reply. Turned into AC 3 (fixed-width reserved slot) and a dedicated unit test.

# Intake Brief — When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G)

## Headline

When a stage filter is applied via `/wl <stage>`, the Pi TUI browse list shows **all** open work items in that stage (standard list order) instead of only the top `browseItemCount` items selected by the `wl next` algorithm.

## Problem Statement

The `/wl <stage>` browse filter (added in WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P) caps the filtered results at `browseItemCount` (default 5) items, selected by the `wl next` priority algorithm. Users who filter by a stage to review its full pipeline see only a curated subset — open items beyond the top 5, or items the `wl next` algorithm deprioritises, are silently missing from the filtered view. Filtering should give a complete picture: every open work item in that stage.

## Users

- Pi TUI users (developers, producers, agents) who use `/wl <stage>` to review everything in a given stage.

### Example User Stories

- As a producer reviewing the pipeline, I want to type `/wl intake_complete` and see **every** open item awaiting planning, not just the top 5, so I know the full workload of that stage.
- As a developer, I want `/wl in_progress` to show all open items currently being worked, including items the `wl next` algorithm ranks lower.
- As an agent planning work, I want `/wl idea` to list all open idea-stage items so none are missed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `/wl <stage>` (canonical name or shorthand alias) shows **all** open work items in that stage — no cap by `browseItemCount` and no omission by the `wl next` selection algorithm.
2. "Open" means `status=open`. Items with status `blocked`, `in-progress`, or `completed` are not shown in the filtered list (even if their stage matches).
3. The filtered list shows root items only; child items remain hidden and are reachable via Tab drill-down exactly as in the unfiltered view.
4. Filtered results are ordered by the standard list order (sortIndex), consistent with the unfiltered browse list.
5. The default `/wl` (no arguments) behaviour is unchanged — it still shows `browseItemCount` items per existing smart-selection logic.
6. Invalid or whitespace-only stage arguments behave as today (error notification + fall back to default unfiltered list, no crash).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Scope is the `/wl <stage>` browse filter in the Pi TUI only.** The CLI `wl list --stage <stage>` output and the default `/wl` view are out of scope.
- **No new settings or flags.** The `browseItemCount` setting continues to govern the unfiltered view only.
- **Shorthand aliases (`intake`, `plan`, `progress`, `review`) keep working unchanged.**
- **Children remain hidden** in the filtered top-level list (consistent with WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR's root-only rule); drill-down is unchanged.

## Existing State

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts`:
  - `createListWorkItemsWithStage(run, count)` runs `wl next -n <count> --stage <stage> --include-in-progress`, normalises the payload, then `.slice(0, itemCount)` — capping at `browseItemCount` and inheriting `wl next`'s algorithm (which hides children and deprioritises items).
  - `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb(count)` uses `db.list({ stage, rootOnly: true })` (no status filter) and `.slice(0, itemCount)`.
- The extension wires the CLI-backed `createListWorkItemsWithStage` as the default in `index.ts` (`const listWorkItemsWithStage = deps.listWorkItemsWithStage ?? createListWorkItemsWithStage();`).
- `wl list` already supports `--status open --stage <stage> --root-only`, returning all open root items in the stage ordered by sortIndex (verified: `intake_complete` → 8 of 10 open items; the 2 excluded are child items).
- Tests live in `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` (stage-filter tests from WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P) and package-level tests under `packages/tui/tests/`.
- Docs: `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` (## `/wl` Slash Command — Stage Filtering) describes the current capped behaviour.

## Desired Change

- In `createListWorkItemsWithStage` (CLI-backed): replace `wl next --stage <stage> -n <count> --include-in-progress` with `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only` and drop the `.slice(0, itemCount)` cap. The `count` parameter becomes unused for the filtered view (or is removed).
- In `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` (DB-backed, kept in sync): add `status: ['open']` to the `db.list` filter and remove the `.slice(0, itemCount)` cap.
- Update/extend tests in `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` to assert: all open root items in the stage are returned (no cap), blocked/in-progress/completed items are excluded, children are excluded but drill-down still works, ordering matches `wl list` sortIndex order, default `/wl` unchanged.
- Update `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` to describe the all-open-items behaviour of stage-filtered views.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/tools.ts` — change `createListWorkItemsWithStage` and `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` to fetch all open root items in the stage (CLI + DB paths).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` — likely no change (stage plumbing already passes the canonical stage through); verify wiring stays intact.
- `tests/extensions/worklog-browse-extension.test.ts` — update stage-filter tests for the new all-items behaviour.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document that stage-filtered views show all open items in that stage.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P — "Add stage-filter arguments to the /wl slash command in the Pi TUI extension"** (completed): Built the `/wl <stage>` filter this item refines (capped at 5 items via `wl next`).
- **WL-0MNUOLCB20008HVX — "Add --stage param to wl next"** (completed): Foundation for stage filtering in `wl next`.
- **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — root-only rule for the Pi TUI browse list** (referenced in code comments): Children hidden from top-level lists; preserved here.
- **WL-0MKW1UNLJ18Z9DUB — "Add TUI search filter using wl list"** (completed): Precedent for using `wl list` output in the TUI.
- **WL-0MP2ISZ8Q008Q19S — "Support comma-separated --status filters in wl list"** (completed): `--status open` filtering on `wl list`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: Behaviour change in ordering.** Filtered views switch from `wl next` priority ordering to sortIndex order. Mitigation: user confirmed standard list order is desired (Appendix); documented in README.
- **Risk: Large stages produce long lists.** A stage with many open items will show them all in one scrollable list. Mitigation: none needed — the browse widget already supports scrolling; keep the list uncapped per AC #1.
- **Risk: DB-backed path diverging from CLI path.** Both `createListWorkItemsWithStage` and `createListWorkItemsWithStageDb` must be updated together or behaviour differs depending on which is wired. Mitigation: update both in the same change; tests cover the CLI-backed default.
- **Assumption:** `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only` semantics are the single source of truth for "all open root items in a stage"; no additional client-side filtering is needed.
- **Assumption:** Child drill-down (Tab) in a filtered view continues to work unchanged (it uses `wl list --parent <id>`, which is stage-agnostic).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Requests for other filter types (priority, assignee) or a configurable filtered-view count should be recorded as new linked work items, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Where should this apply?" — Answer (user): "(a) Only the `/wl <stage>` browse filter in the Pi TUI" (not the CLI `wl list --stage` output). Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "What counts as 'open work items' in a stage?" — Answer (user): "all open only, children can be expanded out as is the case in the unfiltered view" — i.e., `status=open` only (no blocked/in-progress/completed); children remain hidden in the top-level list but reachable via Tab drill-down, same as the unfiltered view. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the default unfiltered `/wl` view also show all open items?" — Answer (user): "the default /wl remains unchanged". Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "Ordering of the filtered results: keep `wl next` priority ordering or standard list order?" — Answer (user): "(b) standard list order (sortIndex), matching the unfiltered view." Source: interactive reply.

# Heartbeat: Surface Audit Progress and Completion Notifications

**Headline:** When the heartbeat dispatches a background audit it is currently invisible — no start signal, no verdict, and silent failure on timeout. This item adds fire-and-forget toasts around the audit invocation plus a durable comment when the audit fails, while keeping heartbeat non-blocking and suppressible for unattended runs.

## Problem statement

The heartbeat skill dispatches audits headlessly (`pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>`) whenever the completed/in_review queue reaches 10+ items. From the producer's perspective this work is invisible: there is no live view, no progress signal, and no notification when the audit lands or when it dies (timeout / non-zero exit). The evaluation in [WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7] identified this as the main visibility gap of headless Pi usage.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want to know when a background heartbeat audit starts, is running, and finishes (with its verdict), without polling the worklog.
- **Operators of unattended environments** (cron, CI, schedulers) — must be able to suppress notifications entirely.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when the heartbeat starts an audit, I want a notification so I know background work is happening."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit completes, I want the verdict (`Ready to close: Yes/No`) surfaced so I don't discover it by chance."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit fails or times out, I want the reason surfaced and recorded, because right now nothing at all is left behind."
- "As an operator running heartbeat from cron, I want to turn notifications off so logs aren't spammed."

## Existing state

- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — runtime copy (Pi resolves the project-local `.pi/skills/` path). Full queue branch selects the first non-ready item by `sortIndex` and runs the audit via `subprocess.run([...], timeout=600)`, discarding stdout; on non-zero exit it returns `"Audit failed for <title> (<id>): <stderr>"`, on `TimeoutExpired` it returns `"Audit timed out for ..."`. No notification of any kind.
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — a **second, separately git-tracked copy** (not a symlink) that has drifted: it dispatches `audit_runner.py` instead of `pi -p`. `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` imports this copy and pins the `.pi` copy's sparse-queue behaviour via `TestPiSkillCopyParity`.
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` and `skill/heartbeat/SKILL.md` — document behaviour, inputs, exit codes; no notification contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` — the established toast plumbing for TS: fire-and-forget `herdr notification show`, default `bottom-right`, tolerant of ENOENT / non-zero exit / `shown: false` / rate-limited `busy`. Requires `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"` in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`.
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md:271` — audit verdicts duplicated into work-item comments are deprecated; the `audit_results` record is the sole consumer of the verdict.

## Desired change

Emit fire-and-forget lifecycle notifications around the audit invocation:

1. **Start** — before spawning the audit subprocess: toast naming the item being audited.
2. **Completion** — after the audit returns: toast with the verdict, derived by re-reading the audit record (`get_audit_result` + `is_ready_to_close`) rather than parsing subprocess stdout.
3. **Failure / timeout** — toast with the reason **and** a durable `wl comment` on the audited item (the reason is recorded nowhere else today). No verdict comment on success, per `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md:271`.

Suppression: `--no-notify` CLI flag **and** `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY=1` env var, plus a silent no-op whenever the `herdr` binary is unavailable or the toast call fails.

Out of scope / unchanged: the sparse-queue branch (flagging the next item with `--needs-producer-review true`), the `sortIndex` selection rule, and the existing stdout message strings — stdout output is retained so the Pi TUI still shows the outcome when the blocking call returns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Dispatching an audit emits a **start** notification naming the audited work item, emitted before the audit subprocess is spawned (unit-tested).
2. A completed audit emits a **completion** notification containing the verdict derived from the audit record (`Ready to close: Yes` / `No`), not from subprocess stdout (unit-tested).
3. An audit that fails (non-zero exit) or times out emits a notification naming the reason **and** adds a `wl comment` recording the failure reason on the audited item; no comment is written on success (unit-tested).
4. Notification delivery is non-blocking and failure-tolerant: a missing `herdr` binary, non-zero exit, or `busy` response never raises and never changes the script's exit code; notifications are suppressed when `--no-notify` is passed or `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY=1` is set (unit-tested).
5. Tests: existing heartbeat unit and integration tests still pass, and new tests cover the start / completion / failure / suppression paths; `TestPiSkillCopyParity` is extended so both copies are asserted to share the notification behaviour.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically `.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` and `skill/heartbeat/SKILL.md` (behaviour, `--no-notify`, `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY`, notification semantics and the herdr `ui.toast.delivery` prerequisite).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Python standard library only — no new dependencies.
- Fire-and-forget delivery: `subprocess.Popen(..., stdio=DEVNULL)` (or equivalent), never blocking the heartbeat, never raising.
- The audit verdict stays authoritative in the `audit_results` record; do not write verdict comments on success (`docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md:271`).
- Preserve the existing exit-code contract: `0` for normal operation including audit failure/timeout messaging, `1` only for `Heartbeat error` (wl command / JSON parse failures).
- Both copies of `heartbeat.py` must stay in parity; the change lands in both.
- Do not build a general notification framework or a Pi-extension live-progress channel here (see Risks: scope-creep).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — Runtime copy. Add notification helpers (fire-and-forget `herdr notification show`, env/flag suppression), emit start/completion/failure notifications around the `pi -p` audit invocation, add `--no-notify`.
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — Canonical/tested copy. Mirror the same notification behaviour and flag so the two copies stay in parity.
- `.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` — Document the notification lifecycle, `--no-notify`, `HEARTBEAT_NO_NOTIFY`, and the herdr `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"` prerequisite.
- `skill/heartbeat/SKILL.md` — Mirror of the same documentation.
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` — New unit tests for start/completion/failure/suppression; extend `TestPiSkillCopyParity` to cover notifications across both copies.
- `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat_integration.py` — Confirm the notification path does not break real `wl` interactions (herdr absent → silent no-op).
- `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` — Reference only (TS equivalent of the Python fire-and-forget helper; no change expected).

## Related work

- `Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane (WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7)` — completed; motivated this item ("Heartbeat audit progress + completion notification ... instead of silent background runs").
- `Create a heartbeat skill for automated work item monitoring (WL-0MRIHB4Q100946QD)` — completed; origin of `heartbeat.py`.
- `Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (WL-0MSACL482002RNYH)` — completed; established `herdr notification show` + `packages/herdr/src/notify.ts` as the toast plumbing.
- `Use centered toast for shortcut feedback instead of status line (WL-0MS7EP7U8008DCXO)` — completed; prior art on toast delivery/rate-limit tolerance.

### Related work (automated find-related report)

**Related work items**
- **WL-0MLG60MK60WDEEGE** — Audit comment improvements (completed)
- **WL-0MVAPF0AD006WHE4** — Complete CLI/API surface: `wl reviewed`, filters, api, completion (completed)
- **WL-0MSACL482002RNYH** — Herdr plugin: use notification system (toasts) instead of bottom-line status updates (completed)

**Repository file matches**
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — toast/notification semantics, `ui.toast.delivery` prerequisite
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — audit dispatch and queue-threshold context
- `CLI.md` — `wl comment` / `wl update` surface used by the notification path

## Risks & assumptions

- **Copy drift (real risk, discovered during intake)** — `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` is a git-tracked duplicate rather than a symlink, and the two copies already dispatch audits differently. Mitigation: implement in both, extend `TestPiSkillCopyParity`; retiring/symlinking the duplicate is a separate candidate item and is **out of scope** here.
- **Toasts can be missed** — herdr rate-limits with `busy` and delivery depends on `ui.toast.delivery = "herdr"`; mitigated by keeping human-readable stdout lines and by the durable failure comment.
- **Verdict freshness** — the completion notification re-reads the audit record after the run. Assumption: a crash before writing the record yields no verdict, which is treated as the failure path (notification + comment).
- **Scope creep** — a Pi-extension-based live progress channel (streaming `pi --mode json` events into the TUI) would be a larger change and is deliberately excluded; record it as a linked item if it becomes desirable.
- **Assumption** — producers watch agent work through herdr, so herdr toasts are the appropriate surface; Pi TUI live notifications are not achievable for a script invoked from a blocking `bash` tool call (`ctx.ui.notify()` is extension-only).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which heartbeat copy is in scope?** (a) implement in `skill/heartbeat` canonical + mirror into `.pi/skills/heartbeat`, extending the parity test; (b) only `.pi/skills/heartbeat`; (c) only `skill/heartbeat`. **Recommended:** (a).
  **Answer (operator):** "A (.pi is not a duplicate, it's a symlink, right?)". **Correction/evidence:** `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` is *not* a symlink — it is a separate git-tracked copy (`git ls-files .pi/skills` → `.pi/skills/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py`; distinct inode 6427255 vs 6298862) that has drifted to a different audit dispatch. Option (a) is therefore implemented as *change both copies, keep them in parity*, and the duplicate is flagged as a candidate follow-up rather than a no-op. Source: interactive reply + repo inspection.
- **Q2: Where does the verdict/failure surface?** (a) toast only; (b) toasts for all three events + durable `wl comment` only on failure/timeout; (c) toast + full verdict comment every completion. **Recommended:** (b).
  **Answer (operator):** "Can't we have it in the Pi TUI with a comment on failure/timeout? if not then b". **Research:** `ctx.ui.notify()` is an extension-only API (`docs/extensions.md`, `docs/tui.md`); heartbeat invokes the audit from a blocking `bash` tool call with a 600 s timeout, so nothing can render in the Pi TUI before the call returns, and there is no external notify API for scripts (`docs/cli-integration.md`: print/JSON/RPC modes only). Live Pi-TUI progress would require streaming `pi --mode json` events via an extension — a larger, separate change. Outcome: **(b) adopted** (toasts for start/completion/failure + `wl comment` on failure/timeout only), with the existing stdout lines retained so the Pi TUI still shows the result when the call returns. Source: interactive reply + Pi docs research.
- **Q3: How do unattended environments suppress notifications?** (a) `--no-notify` flag + silent no-op when `herdr` is unavailable; (b) env var only; (c) both flag and env var + silent no-op. **Recommended:** (a).
  **Answer (operator):** "c". Source: interactive reply.

# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Summary

Deferred follow-up for WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K (Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime). When the llama-proxy serves per-slot details (`slot_id` + `is_processing`) in `GET /llama/local/status` (proxy feature request **LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39**), the herdr downtime worker must track idle duration **per slot identity** so a configured `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N < total slots requires the *same* slot(s) free for the full threshold — not any N slots.

discovered-from:WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K

## User stories

- As an operator, when I configure the downtime worker to require fewer than all slots free (e.g. 2 of 6), I want the same slot(s) to remain free for the full idle threshold so dispatch reflects genuine capacity stability, not transient any-N-slot availability.

## Expected behaviour

- Worker parses optional per-slot fields (`slots: [{slot_id, is_processing}]`) from `/llama/local/status` when present.
- When `downtimeRequiredFreeSlots` N < total slots: idle-duration is tracked per `slot_id`; a slot that starts processing resets its own idle timer; dispatch fires only when the same N slots have been continuously free for ≥ `downtimeIdleThresholdMs`.
- When per-slot data is absent: fail closed to the default all-slots-free condition (the behavior delivered by WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K) — never "any N slots" without same-slot identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the proxy response includes per-slot details, the worker requires the same N slots free for the full threshold; a slot starting processing resets that slot's idle timer.
- [ ] When per-slot details are absent (LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 not fulfilled), the worker degrades to all-slots-free (identical to the current-item behavior) and never dispatches on "any N slots".
- [ ] Unit tests cover per-slot idle tracking, slot-identity reset, and the no-per-slot-data fallback.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes (vitest for packages/herdr).
- [ ] README documents the per-slot behaviour and the N < total slots configuration.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by:LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 (proxy must expose per-slot fields first)
- Blocks/extends WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K AC2 (same-slot stability)

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — extend idle tracker with per-slot_id tracking
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — per-slot tests
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document per-slot behaviour

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q7 (from planning of WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K): "Should same-slot tracking be implemented now against future proxy fields, or deferred until LP-0MSG5TA7Y002GN39 lands?" — Answer (user): "(b) defer; create a follow-up work item". This item is that follow-up.

## Problem

During the excessive-spawn investigation (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J) and in normal operation, `worklog.db-wal` grows large under concurrent writer load (16MB WAL observed). Worklog uses SQLite in WAL mode by design (`src/persistent-store.ts` sets `journal_mode = WAL` for concurrency).

Observations:

- Writes land in `worklog.db-wal` first; `worklog.db` mtime/size stays unchanged until a checkpoint merges the WAL back. A 66KB `worklog.db-wal` was observed in `open_source_llm/.worklog` while `worklog.db` sat untouched — and the WAL files disappear once all processes close (checkpoint on close / auto-checkpoint).
- Under the spawn storm (206 concurrent wl processes), the WAL reached ~16MB, meaning auto-checkpointing was not keeping up with write volume.

Why this matters:

1. **Read cost:** SQLite reads must scan the WAL, so a large WAL slows every read query.
2. **Cache invalidation:** mtime/size of `worklog.db` alone is unreliable while a large WAL holds live writes (see WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 AC #2 — cache must be WAL-aware).
3. **Crash/recovery:** a large WAL means longer recovery time on abnormal exit.

## Goals

- Understand current checkpointing behavior: default auto-checkpoint threshold, when/where wl checkpoints (per-write? on close? explicit wal_checkpoint?), and how concurrent writers interact.
- Determine whether a large-WAL state is a correctness risk or only a performance cost.
- Decide if wl should checkpoint after write batches (e.g., after `wl sync` or bulk mutations) or rely on auto-checkpoint.

## Suggested approach

- Inspect `src/persistent-store.ts` and `src/database.ts` for pragma settings and any checkpoint logic.
- Reproduce: run N concurrent write processes against one worklog and measure WAL growth, read latency, and checkpoint behavior.
- Consider adding an explicit `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE/TRUNCATE)` after write-heavy operations if evidence supports it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Documented understanding of when/where checkpointing happens and why a 16MB WAL occurred (root cause identified, reproduced, or ruled out).
2. Measured impact of large WAL on read latency (before/after numbers).
3. A recommendation recorded on this item: leave as-is, add explicit checkpointing, or tune auto-checkpoint threshold — with rationale and risk notes.
4. Any code change is tested and does not regress the full test suite.

discovered-from:WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3

# Herdr selection list: shortcut hint bar empty until a chord key is pressed

## Problem statement

In the Herdr "Worklog Selection List" pane (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), the footer hint bar that shows the available shortcut commands (e.g. `c:create new  i:implement  u:update...  x:close...`) is empty when the list opens. The hints only appear after the user presses the first key of a chord (e.g. `u`), at which point a `chord: u _ ...` footer renders. The behavior is inconsistent: the initial hints are gated behind the `showHelpText` plugin setting, but the chord-in-progress footer is not gated by it.

## Users

Herdr users who run the Worklog Selection List pane and rely on the footer hint bar to discover keyboard shortcuts.

- As a user opening the Worklog Selection List, I want to see the available shortcut commands in the hint bar immediately, so I know which keys are available without pressing them first.
- As a user who has deliberately disabled help text, I want the setting to behave consistently (all hint lines hidden, including chord-mode hints), matching the pi browse widget.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `showHelpText` on (the default), the footer hint bar shows the available shortcut commands as soon as the selection list opens — before any chord key is pressed. (No change to the current on-state rendering.)
2. With `showHelpText` off, the chord-in-progress footer (`chord: <keys> _ <hints>`) is also hidden, so no shortcut hints render in any mode — consistent with the pi browse widget's `showHelpText` handling.
3. The `showHelpText` default remains `true` in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (`defaultSettings`), `loadSettings()` fallback, and `runWorklistTui` options; verify no code path silently defaults it to `false`.
4. The user's local Herdr config (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) is set so `showHelpText` is `true` (or the key is removed to fall back to the default), restoring the visible hint bar for the reporter.
5. Automated tests cover: (a) chord-mode footer suppressed when `showHelpText` is `false`, and (b) chord-mode footer present when `showHelpText` is `true`/unset. Full project test suite passes.
6. Documentation is updated to reflect the change: the Herdr README's `showHelpText` description (`packages/herdr/README.md`) accurately states that `false` hides all shortcut hint lines, including chord-mode hints; code comments on the renderer footer and call site explain the gating.

## Constraints

- Keep the `showHelpText` setting; do not remove or repurpose it (operator decision C).
- The Herdr plugin reads settings from `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` (via `loadSettings()`); the repo must not depend on the reporter's local config for tests.
- The chord key *handling* (state machine) must keep working even when the hint footer is hidden — only rendering is affected.
- Backward compatibility for `createListRenderer` callers: adding a renderer parameter must not break existing tests that call it positionally.

## Existing state

- The initial shortcut hints are computed as `dynamicHints` in `runWorklistTui` and passed to the renderer only when `opts.getShowHelpText()` is true (`worklist.ts` ~line 2666: `opts.getShowHelpText() ? dynamicHints : undefined`).
- The renderer footer (`createListRenderer`, `worklist.ts` ~lines 1683–1697) has two branches:
  - chord active (`chordState.pendingKeys.length > 0`): always renders `chord: <keys> _ <hints>` using `chordState.hints` — **not** gated by `showHelpText`.
  - otherwise: renders `[esc] back` nav hint plus `chordHelpHints` — gated by `showHelpText` at the call site.
- With the reporter's config `showHelpText: false` this yields: empty footer on open; `chord: u _ update...` footer once a chord key is pressed — exactly the reported behavior.
- The pi browse widget (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) gates the entire help line (including chord hints `🔗 …`) behind `currentSettings.showHelpText` — consistent, and the reference behavior for this fix.
- The reporter's local config `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` currently contains `"showHelpText": false`.

## Desired change

1. Gate the chord-in-progress footer in the renderer behind `showHelpText` so `showHelpText: false` hides all hint lines (normal and chord-mode), matching the pi widget.
   - Suggested approach: add a trailing `showHelpText` parameter to `createListRenderer`'s returned renderer (defaulting to `true` when `undefined`, preserving existing positional callers/tests), render the chord footer only when `isChordActive && showHelpText`, and pass `opts.getShowHelpText()` from `runWorklistTui`'s call site.
2. Add/extend renderer tests covering the chord-footer gating above (see AC 5).
3. Update the reporter's local `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` so `showHelpText` is `true` (or remove the key), restoring the visible hint bar.

## Risks & assumptions

- The chosen behavior (C) means users with `showHelpText: false` get **no** visual chord feedback at all (not even `chord: u _`). This matches the pi widget but is a UX tradeoff — documented in the README update (AC 6).
- Chord key *handling* must keep working with the footer hidden; the fix must only affect rendering. Guard with a test that chord state still accumulates while `showHelpText` is `false`.
- Adding a trailing `showHelpText` param to `createListRenderer` must not break existing positional callers/tests (default `true` when `undefined`).
- The reporter's local config fix (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) is out-of-repo; the implementing agent cannot commit it — it must be applied locally (AC 4) or the key removed to use the default.
- Scope-creep guard: adjacent renderer/footer improvements (e.g., "items below the fold" — WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ) are separate work items; do not expand scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` footer branch: gate chord-mode footer behind `showHelpText`; `runWorklistTui` call site: pass `opts.getShowHelpText()` to the renderer.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — new tests: chord footer hidden when `showHelpText: false`; chord footer shown when `true`/unset.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — verification only: confirm `showHelpText` default stays `true`.
- `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` — local (out-of-repo) change: set `showHelpText` to `true`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MS4FJ2TX009V7V5` — "Rich settings: browseItemCount and showHelpText toggle" (completed): introduced the `showHelpText` setting for Herdr; commit `d637c9b2` gated the initial help hints but left the chord footer ungated — the root of this inconsistency.
- `WL-0MS3ANM1H007SG92` — "Rich settings for Herdr plugin: browseItemCount and showHelpText" (completed): companion/parent settings work.
- `WL-0MS31Q7FD00710B7` — "Chord shortcut system & dynamic help bar" (completed): the chord system + help bar this issue touches.
- `WL-0MQEBM6OM004Q1Q7` — "Chord dispatch and help text in browse views" (completed): chord/help-text behavior in the pi browse views (the consistency reference).
- `WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ` — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (open): separate issue on the same renderer/component (`createListRenderer`); may touch adjacent footer/list-area code.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the desired end state be? A) hint bar always shows regardless of `showHelpText` (remove/repurpose the setting); B) keep the setting and set the config to `true`; C) keep the setting and fix the inconsistency — `showHelpText` off hides *all* hints including chord-mode ones (consistent with the pi widget)."
  - Answer (operator): "C — on by default." Source: interactive reply.
  - Interpretation: keep the `showHelpText` setting; gate the chord-mode footer behind it so `false` hides all hint lines; the setting default must remain `true` (it already is in `settings.ts` `defaultSettings`, `loadSettings()` fallback, and `runWorklistTui` options — verification-only AC 3). The reporter's local config currently overrides the default to `false`, so it must be flipped to `true` (or the key removed) for the hint bar to be visible again (AC 4).
  - Note: chord key *handling* must remain functional with the footer hidden; only rendering is affected.

# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The work item selection list header shows the plugin version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json`), right-aligned to the pane width.
2. The version is rendered in the dimmed ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the existing `[auto-refresh on]` treatment, and does not interfere with the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title.
3. The version is read at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` (not hardcoded in the renderer), so it stays in sync with the manifest version.
4. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover the header rendering with the version suffix, including a case without a version available (graceful fallback).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unobtrusive: dimmed font, right-aligned to the pane edge; must not change existing header content or alignment of the title.
- Use existing patterns: `termSize.cols` for pane width, `ANSI.dim` for dimming, `readFileSync` for reading `package.json` (pattern already used in `worklist.ts`/`shortcut-config.ts`).
- No changes to `herdr-plugin.toml` version unless a version bump is explicitly requested.
- Do not update CHANGELOG.md (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The selection list header is rendered in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~line 1585): ` Work Items — N item(s)` plus optional `[auto-refresh on]` (dimmed) and `[paused — hidden]` indicators.
- `termSize` (with `cols`) is available in the render function; `truncateLine()` handles width overflow.
- The plugin version is declared in two places: `packages/herdr/package.json` (`"version": "0.1.0"`) and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`). There is currently no runtime version constant.
- Existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86–100) assert `'Work Items'` presence.

## Desired change

1. Add a runtime helper that reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (e.g., parse JSON, fall back to a safe default like `'?'` or omit when unreadable).
2. In the list-mode header renderer, append a dimmed `v<version>` string right-aligned to `cols` (using padding), while keeping the title left-aligned.
3. Add unit tests covering: version suffix present and right-aligned, dim style applied, graceful fallback when the version can't be read.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering; add version read + right-aligned dimmed suffix (near line 1585).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Header assertions for version suffix, alignment, and fallback.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — Version source (`0.1.0`); no change expected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Optional: document the version display.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr: parent feature that produced `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **WL-0MQHYI4E60075SQT** — Fix icon prefix alignment in Pi TUI work item selection list: related header/line formatting work (Pi TUI counterpart).
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus: related Herdr list behavior work.
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** — Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension: related footer/status UI precedent (Pi TUI counterpart).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ34IDI0XTA5TB** – TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** – Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, src, using, version, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2-enforce-git-worktree-usage-for-all-imple/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `package.json` is present next to the compiled/tsx module at runtime; the module-dir relative read pattern (as in `shortcut-config.ts`) works for both `npx tsx` and `dist` runs.
- **Risk**: ANSI codes in a right-padded line can misalign padding calculations if padding is computed on raw text length; must compute visible-width padding before applying ANSI styles.
- **Risk**: Very narrow panes could crowd the header; the version suffix should be dropped or truncated if it would overlap the title (guard on `cols`).
- **Scope creep risk**: Bumping the version, adding the version elsewhere (footer/status bar), or showing `wl`/ContextHub versions — out of scope; record as follow-up work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Which version number? I assume the plugin's own version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml`) — or did you mean the `wl` CLI version or ContextHub's version?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes the plugins" — the Worklog Selection List plugin's own version. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2**: "Placement preference? Unobtrusive, dimmed — candidates: (a) right side of the header line, (b) footer hint line, (c) bottom-right corner."  
  **Answer** (user): "a (right aligned to width of pane)" — right-aligned in the header line. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief — Insert selected work-item ID into herdr command input forms (WL-0MSGPSEFW006VINF)

## Problem statement

When typing a free-form prompt in a herdr command input form (e.g. the `P-p` chord, which opens a prompt sent to a new Pi agent pane), there is no discoverable way to reference the currently selected work item by its ID. The `<id>` magic token already works inside form field values (both chord and single-key form paths in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolve it to the selected item's ID on submit), but the behavior is undocumented, untested, and invisible in the UI — and in one edge case (no item selected, `P-p` path) a literal `<id>` leaks through to Pi.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who open the `P-p` free-form prompt (or any chord form) and want the prompt to reference the work item they currently have selected — without memorising/pasting the ID.
- **Pi agents / operators** who receive the prompt — the prompt becomes self-contained with the item ID, so no follow-up lookup is needed.

User stories:
- As a Herdr user with an item selected in the worklist, I want to type `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt so the selected item's ID is inserted into the prompt sent to Pi.
- As a Herdr user filling any chord command form (e.g. `u-t` title, `u-s` stage), I want `<id>` to resolve to the currently selected item's ID the same way it does in command templates.
- As a new Herdr user, I want the form dialog to hint that `<id>` is available, so I don't need to read the README to discover it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt field inserts the currently selected work item's ID into the prompt text sent to Pi (verified by an automated regression test on the form-submit path; no new `wl` spawn needed).
2. The same `<id>`-in-field behavior works in **all** herdr command input forms, for both the chord and single-key dispatch paths.
3. The form dialog renders a discoverability hint (e.g. a footer/help line such as "type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") whenever the form is shown.
4. When no work item is selected and a form field value contains `<id>`, the behavior is graceful and consistent across all paths — no literal `<id>` is sent to Pi; the documented decision (see Risks & assumptions) is implemented and covered by a test.
5. `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the `<id>`-in-form-field behavior, including the `P-p` free-prompt example.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; new tests cover the free-prompt case, the generic form case, the no-item-selected edge case, and the discoverability hint.

## Constraints

- **No change to `<id>` handling in command templates** — the existing `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS` / `substituteIdentifiers` mechanism in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` stays as-is.
- **No changes to the chord definitions** in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (P-p, P-a, u-*, etc. remain bound exactly as today).
- No modal/UX overhaul of the form dialog — the hint is a minimal addition to the existing form render.
- All work tracked in wl; no changes to work-item tracking tooling.

## Existing state

- `P-p` chord → `/prompt:<prompt>` opens the command input form (`FormState` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`); on submit the resulting command routes through `worklist.ts` and spawns a Pi agent pane with the bare prompt text (`stripAgentPromptPrefix` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS = {'id'}` in `form-dialog.ts` — `<id>` never triggers an unknown-identifier prompt; `substituteIdentifiers` leaves `<id>` intact in field values.
- Both form onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts` (chord-complete path ~line 2353 and single-key path ~line 2464) replace `<id>` with the selected item's ID via `flat[idx].id`.
- No regression test covers `<id>` typed inside a form field value; no UI hint; README documents `<id>` resolution for command templates only, not for field values/free prompts.
- Edge case: in the form paths, when no item is selected and the field value contains `<id>`, `finalCmd` keeps the literal `<id>` and it is sent (visible to Pi in the `P-p` case); the non-form `executeResolvedCommand` path instead returns a graceful `noop` when `<id>` is in the command and nothing is selected — inconsistent.

## Desired change

- **Verify + formalise the existing mechanism**: add regression tests asserting `<id>` in a form field value resolves to the selected item's ID, for the free prompt (P-p) and generic forms, across chord and single-key paths.
- **Discoverability**: render a hint line in the form dialog ("type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") and document the behavior in `packages/herdr/README.md` (including the `P-p` free-prompt example).
- **Graceful no-item-selected handling**: decide and implement one consistent behavior for `<id>` in field values when nothing is selected (proposed: drop the command with a toast, matching the existing `noop` convention for template `<id>`; documented in the work item).
- **No new mechanism** — the magic-token approach was chosen in intake (option a); chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts were considered and explicitly out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — render the `<id>` discoverability hint in the form dialog (footer/help line); unchanged substitution logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the two form onSubmit callbacks: consistent no-item-selected handling (drop + toast); no change to existing `<id>` resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for `<id>`-in-field resolution, the no-item-selected edge case, and the hint rendering.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document `<id>` inside form field values / free prompts.

## Related work

- **Herdr shortcuts: P-p free prompt and P-a audit-gaps prompt (WL-0MSGHNTMF000YKRI)** — completed; introduced the `P-p` chord this feature builds on.
- **Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)** — completed; `/prompt:` routing + `send-to-pi.sh` pane spawning.
- **Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK)** — completed; introduced `FormState` / form-dialog.
- **Shortcuts with multiple <id> tokens only replace the first occurrence (WL-0MRNLF5UO0088ID2)** — completed; multiple-`<id>` handling relevant to the `u-t`/`u-s` edge case.
- **Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)** — completed; text-insertion template wiring in the same code area.
- **Related work (automated report, /skill:find-related)** — additional matches retained as lower-priority context: **wl sync timeouts (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR)** (completed; herdr auto-sync spawn/timeout context), **[test-failure] send-to-pi.sh / open-pi-agent.sh pane-launch tests (WL-0MSGAKL8R009GB1X)** (completed; pane-launch regression relevant to the P-p spawn path), **Unify dialog widget construction and layout helpers (WL-0MNX4D4G8009XZNJ)** (completed; form-dialog rendering helpers). Automated repo-file matches (audit_runner.py, intake SKILL.md) were reviewed and dropped — generic keyword noise from the wrong repo root.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-implementation risk:** the mechanism already exists; the main risk is building a redundant insertion mechanism instead of testing + surfacing the existing magic token. Mitigation: scope is verification, discoverability, and edge-case handling only.
- **No-item-selected edge case:** proposed default = drop the command with a toast (consistent with template `<id>` noop convention). Assumption: users prefer a clear "no item selected" signal over sending a literal `<id>` to Pi.
- **Multi-`<id>` forms (`u-t` title, `u-s` stage):** typing `<id>` into such a field replaces every `<id>` in the command (target and field value) with the selected ID — existing multiple-`<id>` behavior, accepted as-is; noted in docs.
- **Scope-creep risk:** chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts (intake options b/c) are out of scope; if requested later, record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** the selected item is the one highlighted in the herdr worklist (`state.selectedIndex`), same source used by all existing `<id>` substitutions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` reference — that ID is an existing, unrelated in-progress work item (the wl read-cache epic). Which did you mean? (a) It was simply the item currently selected in your herdr pane — the feature is generic: insert *whatever* item is currently selected. (b) It should be a magic token: typing that literal string into the prompt gets replaced with the currently selected item's ID before sending. (c) Something else." — Answer (operator): "a" — generic; insert whatever item is currently selected. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Insertion mechanism — how should the ID get into the input box while typing? (a) A magic token in the prompt text (e.g. typing `<id>` — consistent with the existing placeholder convention in herdr commands). (b) A chord/keypress *inside* the input box (e.g. a key or chord that pastes the selected ID at the cursor). (c) Open the P-p prompt pre-filled with the selected ID. (d) Freeform." — Answer (operator): "a" — magic token (`<id>`). Source: interactive reply. Note: (b) and (c) explicitly out of scope.
- Q3: "Scope — which input boxes should support this? (a) Only the herdr P-p free-prompt input box. (b) All herdr command input forms. (c) Also the main pi prompt input (the `P` key in the pi TUI) — note: that lives in pi core and may not be reachable from a herdr plugin extension." — Answer (operator): "b" — all herdr command input forms. Source: interactive reply. Note: pi core input out of scope.
- Q4 (agent research note, no user answer required): does typing `<id>` in a form field already work? — Research: inspected `form-dialog.ts` (`KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS`, `substituteIdentifiers`) and both onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts`; the mechanism already resolves `<id>` to the selected item's ID on submit in both chord and single-key paths. No test covers this path; no UI hint; `P-p` with no item selected leaks literal `<id>` to Pi. Findings incorporated into Existing state / Desired change.

## Summary

`wl next` (and `wl next -n <count>`) currently returns items whose stage is `done`, wasting fetch budget and polluting top-N work lists. Verified: `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returned 20 items of which **12 had stage=done** (e.g. WL-0MMKENAJT14229DE, WL-0MMTDALZO0KQEZMI). Downstream consumers (herdr worklist `fetchNextItems`, pi TUI) then must filter them out client-side, and the TUI fetch budget is effectively reduced (herdr showed 9 items instead of 20 because 12 of the fetched 20 were done).

## User story

As an operator using wl next or a TUI that consumes it, I want done items excluded from results so that the top-N list is full of actionable work and no downstream filtering is needed.

## Expected behaviour

- `wl next` returns only non-done items by default (stage not in [done]).
- `wl next -n 20` returns up to 20 actionable items.
- The `--stage done` filter still allows explicitly requesting done items (filter semantics unchanged: stage filters remain explicit opt-in).
- Existing behaviour for other stages/statuses unchanged; dependency-blocked and in-progress handling unchanged.

## Implementation notes

- Likely in the `next` command implementation (src/commands/next.ts in ContextHub, which is also the global worklog CLI via npm link).
- Add an exclusion predicate for stage=done in the default (unfiltered) query path, similar to how status filters are applied.
- Check existing tests (tests/commands/next.test.ts or similar) and add coverage: a done item is excluded by default, included with explicit --stage done.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returns zero items with stage=done.
- [ ] `wl next --stage done -n 5` still returns done items.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover the exclusion and the explicit --stage done opt-in.
- [ ] herdr worklist pane no longer needs its client-side stage=done filter (may be kept as defensive).

# Add shortcut to return to the default browse view

## Headline

From a stage-filtered browse list (e.g. `/wl in_progress`), the chord `f s` (sprint) returns the user to the default unfiltered browse list (equivalent to `/wl` with no arguments), instead of requiring Esc to close the widget and re-invoking `/wl`.

> **Scope note (2026-08-08):** The Pi TUI browse UI was removed from this repo (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N). The `/wl` command and its shortcut chords now live in the **Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr`). This work item's implementation was therefore delivered in `packages/herdr` — see Key Files below. AC6 (README docs) refers to `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Problem Statement

Currently there is no way to navigate from a stage-filtered list back to the default view without closing the browse widget entirely. The filter chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`) are one-way: they switch to a filtered list but nothing switches back.

## Users

- Herdr plugin users who use `/wl <stage>` filters and want to return to the standard next-items list without re-invoking the command.

### Example User Stories

- As a developer, I want to press `f s` while viewing `/wl in_progress` to return to the default next-items browse list.
- As a producer, I want the back-to-default action to be discoverable in the shortcut help line.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pressing the chord `f s` (label: sprint) from any stage-filtered browse list returns the user to the default unfiltered browse list (equivalent to `/wl` with no arguments).
2. The chord is visible in the browse help line with the label `sprint`.
3. All existing shortcut chords continue to work — `f n` remains bound to 'filter intake' (/wl intake); no existing binding is changed.
4. The default `/wl` (no arguments) behaviour is unchanged.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. README shortcut documentation (`packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut chord list) is updated to document the `f s` sprint chord.

## Constraints

- Scope is the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — the Pi TUI Worklog browse extension was removed from the repo (WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N).
- Implementation follows the existing config-driven shortcut system (`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`) — no hardcoded key handlers.

## Existing State

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` defines all shortcut chords. Current `f`-chords: `f i`=idea, `f n`=intake, `f p`=plan, `f r`=review. `f s` is free (verified).
- Chord dispatch (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) resolves chords via `shortcuts.json` and executes the resolved command; `/wl <stage>` filters the browse list by stage; `/wl` with no stage argument returns to the default unfiltered list.

## Desired Change

- Add to `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`:
  ```json
  { "chord": ["f", "s"], "command": "/wl", "view": "both", "label": "sprint", "description": "Return to the default unfiltered browse list." }
  ```
- Verify chord dispatch: pressing `f s` in the list view resolves to command `/wl`, which clears any stage filter and opens the default browse flow.
- Update `packages/herdr/README.md` shortcut documentation to list the new `f s` sprint chord.
- Add/extend tests in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` / `worklist.test.ts` asserting the `f s` chord exists, is registered, resolves to `/wl`, and does not conflict with existing bindings.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — the `f s` sprint chord entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `/wl <stage>` dispatch, stage map, clearFilter (`/wl` no-args).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchItemsByStage` (stage-filtered list, root-only, open status).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — documents the `f s` sprint chord and stage-filtered browse views.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — tests for the new chord.

## Related Work

- discovered-from:WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G (stage-filtered browse list work)
- WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P — /wl stage filter (parent feature)
- WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N — Pi TUI removal (feature moved to Herdr)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Which resolution for the `f n` collision?" — Answer (user): "use f s (sprint)" — keep `f n` = filter intake; bind back-to-default to `f s` with label 'sprint'. Verified `f s` is free. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-06.
